title: Stucco Cracks in Lake City Homes: Causes and Fixes
description: Why stucco cracks on Lake City and Columbia County homes, which cracks are cosmetic, and how to patch and coat them so repairs last through the wet season.
excerpt: Why stucco cracks on Lake City homes, how to tell cosmetic from structural, and how to patch and coat so repairs last.
h1: Stucco Cracks in Lake City Homes: Causes and Fixes
heroIntro: Stucco cracks are one of the most common exterior questions from Lake City and Columbia County homeowners. Most are manageable, but the ground under the house and the way water moves around it decide whether a repair lasts.

questions: Why does stucco crack on Lake City homes?
Are stucco cracks a foundation problem?
How do you fix stucco cracks before painting?

body: Stucco is a rigid cement plaster. It handles compression well but has very little ability to stretch, so anything that moves the wall even slightly shows up as a crack. Around Lake City, three forces do most of the work.
bullets: Seasonal soil movement: soils in parts of Columbia County contain clay layers that swell when soaked and shrink as they dry. The long wet season followed by drier months moves foundations and slabs slightly, and the stucco above records it.
Thermal cycling: hot afternoon sun followed by cooler nights expands and contracts the wall daily, especially on south and west elevations.
Shrinkage and stress at openings: stucco shrinks as it cures, and corners of windows and doors concentrate stress, which is why diagonal cracks so often start there.

body: Most cracks on Lake City homes are fine hairlines or short diagonals at openings, and they are cosmetic. They may open slightly in dry months and close up during the rains, which is normal movement rather than failure. A few patterns call for caution, especially when you see more than one of them on the same wall:
bullets: Cracks wider than about 1/8 inch, or cracks you can see growing over weeks
One side of the crack sitting higher or further out than the other
Stair-step cracks running through block joints beneath the stucco
New interior cracks, doors that start to stick, or windows that bind
Stucco that sounds hollow or bulges around the crack

body: Mark the ends of a crack with a pencil and the date, measure its width with a ruler or crack gauge, and check again after a heavy rain and after a dry spell. If it is stable, a cosmetic repair is appropriate. If it is moving or shows the warning signs above, have a structural engineer or a qualified foundation professional look at it before any coating goes on. North Florida’s karst geology is another reason not to dismiss unusual cracking.

sections.h2: How to repair stucco cracks that last
bullets: Wash the wall gently to remove dirt, chalk, and mildew; avoid high pressure that erodes stucco.
Measure the crack width; this determines the repair material.
For hairlines, brush in an elastomeric crack filler and feather it flush.
For wider static cracks, open into a shallow V, clean, and fill with a stucco patch; for moving joints, use a flexible, paintable sealant.
For recurring cracks, embed fiberglass mesh in a base coat across the repair.
Match the surrounding texture so the patch disappears.
Prime repairs as directed, then apply an elastomeric coating rated for the crack width you measured, at the specified thickness.
body: The sequence below is the one that holds through a Columbia County wet season. Matching the coating to the measured crack width is the step most often skipped.

Elastomeric wall coatings form a thick, flexible film that can bridge hairline cracks and stretch as the wall moves, which is why they are often the right finish for stucco with ongoing hairline movement. Each product is rated for the crack size it can bridge, and that rating assumes it goes on at full thickness, so thin application defeats the purpose. Because elastomerics are less breathable than standard acrylics, the wall must be dry and sound first. Where cracking is not an issue, a quality 100% acrylic is often the better fit. Our general guide to stucco crack repair goes deeper on crack patterns.

sections.h2: What a stucco repaint project involves
body: When cracks are stable and the wall is ready for a refresh, a well-run stucco repaint in Lake City generally follows the same arc. Knowing it helps you compare estimates and spot shortcuts.

It starts with a walkthrough to map cracks, check for hollow or loose stucco, and take moisture readings where staining or blistering suggest water. Then comes a low-pressure wash and mildew treatment, followed by drying time, which in the humid months can take longer than people expect. Crack repairs and texture matching come next, then priming of patches and any bare masonry. Finally, the coating goes on in full coats, and sprayed coats are back-rolled so the material works into the texture instead of skimming over it.

Plan on more than a one-day job. A full exterior typically takes several working days plus washing and dry time, and weather can shift the schedule. Patches and fresh coatings both need dry conditions to cure properly, so a good crew will pause rather than coat a damp wall.

Since soil moisture swings drive much of the cracking, controlling water around the foundation is the best prevention. Extend downspouts so they discharge several feet from the house, keep the grade sloping away from the walls, and keep irrigation off the base of the stucco. Clear gutters before the summer rainy season. After each wet season, walk the house and check your pencil marks; catching a new crack early keeps it a small repair. Keeping the paint film intact matters too, since bare, chalky stucco absorbs water and cycles harder. Trees planted close to the house can also draw moisture unevenly from the soil near the foundation, so consider root zones when you plan new landscaping, and keep heavy shrubs a few feet from the walls so the stucco can dry after rain.

faqs.q: Are stucco cracks on my Lake City home a foundation problem?
faqs.a: Usually not. Most are hairline or corner cracks from shrinkage and normal movement. Wide, growing, or offset cracks, stair-step patterns, or sticking doors should be evaluated by a structural professional.

faqs.q: Why do stucco cracks come back after painting?
faqs.a: Regular paint cannot stretch with a moving crack. Fill the crack correctly, add mesh where cracks recur, and use an elastomeric coating rated for the measured crack width.

faqs.q: When is the best time to repair stucco in Lake City?
faqs.a: Fall through spring generally offers drier, milder conditions for patching and coating. Summer work is possible with early starts that avoid afternoon storms.

faqs.q: Can I fix hairline stucco cracks myself?
faqs.a: Yes, small hairlines on a single-story wall are a reasonable DIY repair with an exterior stucco crack filler. Larger areas, wider cracks, and work at height are better handled by a pro.
